newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper seen vulnerable to downside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper seen vulnerable to downside.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper faces resistance at $2,500 after this week's downside correction and is vulnerable to the test of recent support around $2,470, analysts said.
Aluminium is also expected to come under pressure following Tuesday's close, they added.
COPPER - The metal's technical picture has been damaged by the downside correction that started on Monday, and copper could re-test trendline support at $2,473, analysts said.

"This market could break either way. On the upside, a breach of $2,502 signals a test of $2,531 and possibly higher, whilst if $2,480 and $2,470 fail to hold, falls to $2,445 and lower are possible," said analyst Harry Creates of Amalgamated Metal Trading Ltd.
Three months copper was last at $2,490, up $11 from Tuesday's kerb close.
ALUMINIUM - Technical and fund selling has been persistently undermining the market. If that continues, the market could take a look below the recent low of $1,575 towards $1,550.
However, a big LME stock drawdown of 4,250 tonnes will be supportive, analysts said.
"The technical picture continues to deteriorate with a bearish cross of the 10- and 30-day averages likely to pressure prices further," brokers Brandeis said in a report.
"However, the RSI, at 32.96, is approaching the oversold portion of the chart."
Three months aluminium was last at $1,580, up $2 from Tuesday's kerb close.
